title: How to Do Great Work

cards.definition_en: Point where two or more things overlap or meet.
cards.example: The intersection of different fields reveals common techniques for great work.
cards.image_prompt: Two colorful ribbons crossing over each other forming a bright intersection, abstract background

cards.definition_en: Having a strong desire to achieve something great.
cards.example: The recipe assumes you're very ambitious.
cards.image_prompt: A person climbing a steep mountain with a flag at sunrise, determined expression

cards.definition_en: Natural ability to do something well.
cards.example: You need something you have a natural aptitude for.
cards.image_prompt: A brain glowing with gears, highlighting a talent spark

cards.definition_en: Edge of known knowledge or exploration.
cards.example: Learn enough to get to the frontier of knowledge.
cards.image_prompt: An explorer standing at the edge of a misty landscape, horizon beyond

cards.definition_en: Something markedly different from the rest.
cards.example: Boldly chase outlier ideas, even if other people aren't interested.
cards.image_prompt: A bright red dot far away from a cluster of blue dots

cards.definition_en: Based on observation or experience rather than theory.
cards.example: The empirical evidence is on the scale of the evidence for mortality.
cards.image_prompt: A scientist holding a clipboard with data charts in a realistic lab setting

cards.definition_en: Careful and persistent work or effort.
cards.example: Interest will drive you to work harder than mere diligence ever could.
cards.image_prompt: A person steadily writing at a desk with a candle, focused

cards.definition_en: Strong desire to learn or know something.
cards.example: The three most powerful motives are curiosity, delight, and the desire to do something impressive.
cards.image_prompt: A child peeking through a magnifying glass at a mysterious object

cards.example: The three most powerful motives are curiosity, delight, and the desire to do something impressive.
cards.image_prompt: A smiling face surrounded by fireworks, feeling joy

cards.definition_en: To come together from different directions.
cards.example: Exciting and important will converge as you grow older.
cards.image_prompt: Multiple arrows pointing toward a single point on a map

cards.definition_en: Make as effective or functional as possible.
cards.example: When in doubt, optimize for interestingness.
cards.image_prompt: A gear system being adjusted to run smoothly, with a checklist

cards.definition_en: Attempt to appear more important or cultured than one is.
cards.example: There are a lot of forces that will lead you astray... pretentiousness, fashion, fear...
cards.image_prompt: A person wearing an oversized crown and fancy clothes, but with a cracked mask

cards.definition_en: Away from the correct path or direction.
cards.example: If you're interested, you're not astray.
cards.image_prompt: A winding road diverging into a dark forest, with a sign pointing 'Correct Path'

cards.definition_en: Additional effort yields progressively smaller benefits.
cards.example: If you work too hard, you'll find diminishing returns.
cards.image_prompt: A graph line rising steeply then flattening, with a tired worker beside it

cards.definition_en: Initial effort needed to start a process.
cards.example: Work has a sort of activation energy, both per day and per project.
cards.image_prompt: A spark igniting a large engine, symbolizing the start of work

quizlet_txt:
intersection	Point where two or more things overlap or meet. — пересечение. E.g.: The intersection of different fields reveals common techniques for great work.
ambitious	Having a strong desire to achieve something great. — амбициозный. E.g.: The recipe assumes you're very ambitious.
aptitude	Natural ability to do something well. — склонность, талант. E.g.: You need something you have a natural aptitude for.
frontier	Edge of known knowledge or exploration. — граница. E.g.: Learn enough to get to the frontier of knowledge.
outlier	Something markedly different from the rest. — отклоняющийся элемент. E.g.: Boldly chase outlier ideas, even if other people aren't interested.
empirical	Based on observation or experience rather than theory. — эмпирический. E.g.: The empirical evidence is on the scale of the evidence for mortality.
diligence	Careful and persistent work or effort. — усердие. E.g.: Interest will drive you to work harder than mere diligence ever could.
curiosity	Strong desire to learn or know something. — любопытство. E.g.: The three most powerful motives are curiosity, delight, and the desire to do something impressive.
delight	Great pleasure or satisfaction. — восторг. E.g.: The three most powerful motives are curiosity, delight, and the desire to do something impressive.
converge	To come together from different directions. — сходиться. E.g.: Exciting and important will converge as you grow older.
optimize	Make as effective or functional as possible. — оптимизировать. E.g.: When in doubt, optimize for interestingness.
pretentiousness	Attempt to appear more important or cultured than one is. — претенциозность. E.g.: There are a lot of forces that will lead you astray... pretentiousness, fashion, fear...
astray	Away from the correct path or direction. — в сторону, сбиться. E.g.: If you're interested, you're not astray.
diminishing returns	Additional effort yields progressively smaller benefits. — убывающая отдача. E.g.: If you work too hard, you'll find diminishing returns.
activation energy	Initial effort needed to start a process. — энергия активации. E.g.: Work has a sort of activation energy, both per day and per project.
